date.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "(ICW) Pre-Fallout Dark Matches!" (16 January 1999).

evidence.source: The fed's own dark-match results sheet, 16 January 1999.
evidence.note: A four-match untelevised warm-up card ahead of that week's Friday Night Fallout Hour.

matches.note: Chris Diorio reversed a whip into an elevated DDT for the pin after kicking out of a tombstone piledriver and a tilt-a-whirl backbreaker.
Stryker recovered from an early flurry to pin Scotty Angel with a powerbomb.
Both women were counted out on the floor after Night missed a suicide dive.
Brad pinned Twin #1 with The Passing Fad while Josh cut off a save from Twin #2.

date.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "(ICW) SUMMER SIZZLER PART [N]!" and its Free-4-All pre-show companions, 1 August 1998 (all parts dated identically by the archive).

evidence.source: The fed's own pay-per-view broadcast script, its first, from the Toronto Skydome, 1 August 1998.
evidence.note: A twelve-match card (two of them pre-show Free-4-All bouts) crowning new Television and Tag Team title matches, one Juniorweight and one North American title defense, and an International Championship main event.

matches.note: D.B. Bugg pinned Failure with a Shakin' Sleeper, then loaded him into his own truck and hit a Raid Bomb in the truck bed.

matches.stipulation: Number-one contender to the ICW Women's Championship
matches.note: Miss Jasmine blindsided Asrael with the Women's title belt from the apron, then hit a Crowning Jewel on both women before pulling Jill Stephenson on top for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Retirement match, no disqualification, no count-out
matches.note: A hardcore brawl through a slew of weapons; Sylkk hit NBK with his own Killer Death Drive onto a garbage can before finishing with a Shoot the Shit Splash.

Andrew Tucker had Damonberry pinned with a standing moonsault when an unidentified interloper (soon revealed as one of the debuting Smith Twins) pulled him off and attacked him; Damonberry retained the ICW Juniorweight Championship by disqualification.
Jack Curtis never appeared; D.B. Bugg attacked Erosion with a chair and a Raid Bomb immediately after the decision.
Annihilation retained after Patras cut off a save attempt; the Island Rats (Bo and T'Chamunga) then jumped both champions at ringside on Khan Troll's orders.

matches.stipulation: Number-one contender to the ICW North American Championship
matches.note: Jack Vars won with the Vars Drop.

Three-way, falls count anywhere. Westside Walavan Powerbombed Sean Christopher for the first pinfall to eliminate him, then Powerbombed Alex Cote (with help from Vincent Estacio distracting the champion) for the second fall and the title.

matches.stipulation: ICW Women's Championship, also determining ownership of Shane Diamond
matches.note: Miss Jasmine won with a rollup while Rain went for a powerslam; also decided ownership of Shane Diamond, whom Rain's own boyfriend had put up as a stake.

matches.stipulation: ICW North American Championship, winner also number-one contender to the ICW International Championship
matches.note: Steve Milla, seated at ringside, swung a folded chair that caught Vitrone in the back of the head (unclear whether by accident); Paseno followed with a belly-to-belly suplex onto a chair for the pin.

matches.stipulation: Grudge steel cage match, special guest referee Vincent Estacio
matches.note: Special guest referee Vincent Estacio, after appearing to favor Beverly for most of the match, hit him with a Sweet Canadian Chin Music superkick, allowing Andrew to pin him.
A brawl through the arena, a bathroom, a concession stand and the parking lot; Diamond won with a German suplex onto the pavement.
The Island Rats (Bo and T'Chamunga) interfered on Rico's behalf, clipping Sweeney's knee to allow the finish.

date.source: The fed's own broadcast script, subject "(ICW) SHOCKFEST '98 PART [N]!" and its Free-4-All pre-show companion, 5 October 1998 (all parts dated identically by the archive).

evidence.source: The fed's own second pay-per-view broadcast script, from the Tokyo Dome, 5 October 1998.
evidence.note: An eleven-match card (two of them pre-show Free-4-All bouts) crowning new Tag Team, Juniorweight and North American champions, an International Championship defense, and a sixty-minute Iron Man main event between the promotion's own president and its top champion-turned-challenger; a planned ten-man elimination match and a six-man weapons cage match both collapsed into backstage brawls before either could begin.

matches.stipulation: Free-4-All pre-show, Barb Wire Baseball Bat/Knight Stick tag match
matches.note: Genocidal Dream won after Makku Torokko, swinging a barbed-wire bat, accidentally struck his own partner Spardo instead of D.Mented.

matches.stipulation: Free-4-All pre-show, ICW Tag Team Championship, Dumpster match
matches.note: Manager Khan Troll had the champions brought to the ring already bound to wheelchairs and beaten by his own attendants; the Island Rats dumped both men straight into the dumpster for the pin, then were confronted by the Perfectly Perfect Duo and the Best of the Best as they left.

To win, a wrestler had to make his opponent say on the microphone that he respected him; Lionheart forced the words out of Henry with a Texas cloverleaf, then played a hidden tape recording of it back after the bell.

matches.stipulation: ICW Juniorweight Championship, Texas Tornado match
matches.note: A brutal brawl through the Tokyo Dome's backstage area, locker rooms, showers and parking lot; Jasmine won with a Crowning Jewel off the hood of a car, becoming the first woman to hold the title.

matches.stipulation: Three-way submission match, number-one contender to the ICW Women's Championship
matches.note: Envy cracked a chair over Linda's ankle and locked in an ankle lock submission for the tap-out.
To win, a wrestler had to tie his opponent to the crucifix hanging above the ring; Grayson piledrove Rico through a table and hooked both of his hands and feet to the crucifix as it was raised.
Essex won with a release German suplex that sent Jack Stone -- the card's own mystery opponent -- off the scaffold and through a stack of tables below.

matches.stipulation: Double Dog Collar match, number-one contender to the ICW Tag Team Championship
matches.note: With all four men chained together by dog collars, the match spent long stretches with each pair simply refusing to fight; the Island Rats interfered late, allowing the Perfectly Perfect Duo to score the pin.

matches.stipulation: ICW North American Championship, ladder match
matches.note: Westside Walavan ran in and knocked champion Jack Vars from the ladder just as he reached the title; Sylkk climbed back up and pulled the belt down himself.
Bryan Blood's own New Age Revolution stablemate Sean Christopher ran in with a barbed-wire bat but Triple X ducked and Blood was struck instead; Triple X finished him with an X-Factor.

matches.stipulation: ICW International Championship, Hell in a Cell
matches.note: Both men climbed a ladder inside the cell before Paseno hoisted Walsh up and hit a Brooklyn Backbreaker off the top for the pin; D.B. Bugg brawled with the champion immediately afterward.

matches.stipulation: Sixty-minute Iron Man match, special guest referee Jax Jordan (not for a title)
matches.note: Special guest referee Jax Jordan -- ICW's own interim president -- struck Pillow with brass knuckles to hand Diamond the deciding fifth fall with seconds left on the clock; the match finished 3 falls to 2.

name: Friday Night Fallout

Pinfall with Tha End.

Pinfall with the Fist of Iron after Lionheart's entrance music distracted Hawkins.
Pinfall with the Future Shock.
matches.note: Main event. The referee declared no countouts and no disqualifications mid-match.

notes: The fed's first broadcast since its reopening, billed as the return of Friday Night Fallout.

name: Friday Night Fallout

date.source: The fed's own broadcast script, "Friday Night Fallout", posted in five parts on 22 March 2002.

Pinfall with A Martyr's End.
Pinfall backstage with Heavy Mentality onto a broken table, after "Marz" Candress pulled Wise off a pin and Bunny Wise came out.
Pinfall with the Smoothkick.
Pinfall with the Lion's Den.

Roll-up while Pietka shouted at the Masked Superstar Jobber at ringside.

Schoolboy after Hawkins's chair rebounded off the top rope into his own face.

Disqualification: the referee saw Starr throw powder in Wise's eyes.
Pinfall after Heavy Mentality through a table from the apron, with "Marz" Candress's interference.
Pinfall with No Remorse from the top turnbuckle.
Pinfall with the Flatliner from the top turnbuckle.

Pinfall with the Starrstruck, a top-rope DDT.
Pinfall with the Smoothkick, feet on the ropes.

Pinfall with Heavy Mentality after DeMasters struck Alexander's knee with a metal object.

Pinfall with the Quickstryke, ending Wise's winning streak.
Pinfall on Keenan after a spike piledriver onto the title belt, Starr having turned to the champion's side.
